steps.title: No hand-written boot script: generic distro boot does it
steps.body:
ST's default U-Boot environment runs U-Boot's generic "distro boot", which searches for `/boot/extlinux/extlinux.conf` and boots whatever it describes. Nothing here is specific to this repository except the contents of that file and the partition flags.

The six steps on the left run in order. The right column shows the file it reads, how to debug a failure, and why one GPT flag matters.

steps.title: 1. U-Boot asks the ROM where it came from
steps.body:
In `arch/arm/mach-stm32mp/stm32mp2/cpu.c`, U-Boot reads the Boot ROM's boot context. For an SD card `boot_device` is `mmc`, and `boot_instance` says which SDMMC controller.

Those two variables decide which device is searched later.

steps.title: 2. After a 1 second countdown the default command runs
steps.body:
`BOOTDELAY=1` gives a one second countdown (any key stops it and gives the prompt `STM32MP> `). `bootcmd_stm32mp` prints `Boot over mmc0!`.

Stopping here is how you debug by hand.

steps.title: 3. Only the device we booted from is tried
steps.body: `include/configs/stm32mp25_st_common.h` sets `boot_targets` to the MMC instance that U-Boot was loaded from, then runs `distro_bootcmd`.

steps.title: 4. Only partitions with the bootable flag are scanned
steps.body:
`part list mmc N -bootable devplist` collects the partitions that have the bootable flag. If there are none, `devplist` is 1: partition 1, which here is BL2 and not a filesystem.

That would make U-Boot search the wrong place and find nothing.

steps.title: 5. It looks for extlinux.conf under two prefixes
steps.body:
For each prefix, `/` and `/boot/`, U-Boot checks whether `<prefix>extlinux/extlinux.conf` exists. If it does, it runs `sysboot`.

If not, it tries `boot.scr.uimg` and `boot.scr`; this repository does not ship one.

steps.title: 6. sysboot reads the file and booti starts the kernel
steps.body:
`sysboot` parses `extlinux.conf`: `LINUX` goes to `kernel_addr_r` `0x8A000000`, `FDT` to `fdt_addr_r` `0x90000000`, and `APPEND` becomes `bootargs`. Then `booti 0x8A000000 - 0x90000000` hands over to Linux.

The `-` in the middle means no ramdisk.

steps.title: The one file this repository writes
steps.body:
`LINUX` is the kernel, `FDT` the device tree and `APPEND` the kernel command line: the root is given as `root=PARTUUID=6d70326b-0000-4000-8000-000000000001` (a partition's unique ID), the console is `ttySTM0,115200`, and `rootwait rw` waits for the card and mounts it read-write.

If these names are wrong, U-Boot cannot load the kernel or Linux cannot find its root.

steps.anchor: If it does not boot, read the log
steps.title: The log tells you which step failed
steps.body:
"Scanning mmc 0:5..." means a partition is being tried, "Found /boot/extlinux/extlinux.conf" means step 5 worked, and "Retrieving file: /boot/Image" means sysboot is loading.

Nothing after "Boot over mmc0!" points to a missing bootable flag, a wrong `boot_instance`, or a rootfs that is not ext4. Stop autoboot and try `part list mmc 0` and `ls mmc 0:5 /boot`.

steps.title: Takeaway: one flag on rootfs makes the whole search work
steps.body:
`scripts/image.sh` sets the GPT attribute LegacyBIOSBootable (bit 2) on the rootfs partition only, and U-Boot's `part list -bootable` reads exactly that bit.

Without it U-Boot would scan partition 1, `fsbla1`, which holds BL2.
